Verified live across two full app relaunches (not just tab switches) -- same verse both times, matching the value read directly off the simulator's on-disk preferences plist. Separately observed, NOT fixed here (pre-existing, outside this ticket's scope): tapping the hero card's 'Sit with this' opens Capture on its plain idle screen instead of pre-seeded with the verse's question as Dwelly's opening message -- `MainTabView.attemptCapture(prompt:)`'s `presetPrompt` plumbing to `CaptureConversationView`'s `initialMessage` doesn't appear to be landing; worth its own ticket if Kell wants it chased.

Title: Build Reassessment/Threshold Engine
Notes: Per-user counter, threshold-based not real-time/edit-triggered. Raised July 23, 2026. UPDATED Aug 31, 2026 (P11 design session): full tier model locked. Validity floor (not quality) gates whether a reflection counts at all - must contain genuine content (real word), not spam/repeated-character junk; low-quality-but-genuine reflections (even one word) still count. Reflective Density (T-127) never gates eligibility - it only modulates how rich/specific the generated narrative can honestly be. Three tiers: 0-2 qualifying reflections = no narrative, soft directional copy only, no visible count/countdown (avoids gameable target). 3-5 qualifying = first narrative unlocks, thin/honest/affirming even off minimal input (e.g. a single word). 6+ qualifying = same narrative deepens/continues - never restarts as a separate narrative. Regeneration/reassessment is NEVER user-triggered (no manual regenerate action anywhere) - runs automatically, most likely checked on app load, against the local qualifying-reflection count; requires connectivity, and if offline when a threshold would fire it simply runs at next opportunity (no error state, no visible retry). Confirmation loop (T-163): 'Yes, that's me' logs silently in the background, no visible confirmation state; 'Not quite' opens a free-text 'What feels off, or what's missing?' field + Submit, feeding the next reassessment cycle, not an instant rewrite. OFFLINE/ONLINE: narrative text itself is generated online via the shared LLM proxy (T-168) - see T-119 note below for budget - then cached locally as read-only content, viewable offline, never locally re-written by the user. Plain Stats are pure local counts, always offline-available (no network dependency, same as Search/T-128). Rhythm, Intent, 'Yes', and 'Not quite' feedback are real user actions - written locally the instant they happen, synced to Supabase in background, same offline-first pattern as saving a Moment. No Pending/offline UI indicator anywhere on Growth, following the P4 precedent that Save always writes locally first. BUILT Nov 16 2026 (rescoped, Kell's direct call): the real engine this ticket describes -- regenerate when there's new qualifying content since the narrative was last written. New DwellerProfileManager.regenerateIfNeeded(...), called from YourNarrativeCard.load() on every appearance (not a separate background job -- immediate and visible, so a user doesn't wait to see feedback land). Threshold stays the already-locked 3 (Aug 31 2026 design session -- 0-2 = no narrative, 3-5 = Tier 1, 6+ deepen is Post-MVP, unchanged). 'Qualifying content' = any approved JournalEntry OR any narrative_feedback row created after the profile's own updated_at; both are weighted identically -- literally the same reflections array fed into the regeneration prompt (see T-164). Confirming ('Yes, that's me') does NOT trigger regeneration (Kell's call, same session) -- it's a log-only signal (T-163's confirmed_at). Verified live end-to-end on a real account (no new account needed): inserted a new narrative_feedback row directly, relaunched the app, and the narrative regenerated automatically on load -- new text genuinely incorporated the feedback's content (anxiety/finances language appeared that wasn't in any prior entry), confirmed_at correctly went stale (older than the new updated_at), Yes/Not-quite buttons reappeared. BUG FOUND + FIXED (same session): Kell asked to run live comparison experiments on real reflection combinations, which surfaced a real data leak -- fetchApprovedJournalEntries never excluded a soft-deleted moment's own journal_entries row (T-158's soft delete only ever filtered moments.deleted_at in fetch-moments' own list query, never here), so a deleted moment's content kept counting toward the qualifying-reflection threshold and kept feeding the narrative forever. Fixed with a PostgREST embedded-resource filter (?select=*,moments!inner(deleted_at)&moments.deleted_at=is.null) -- verified against this account's real data (an entry whose moment was soft-deleted correctly dropped out, count went from 8 to the correct 7, matching Plain Stats).

Title: Reconcile Pillar 9 Notification Preferences Screen with Pillar 8 Notification Strategy
Notes: Raised Aug 28, 2026: a Notifications 'Manage Preferences' screen was designed and built in Figma (both MVP and Post-MVP) under Pillar 9 (Account Profile) - 3 modes (Default/Sparse/Off) + Sabbath/Quiet Days toggle with per-day selection - before checking it against Pillar 8's actual locked notification architecture. Needs a design pass to confirm: (1) does the simple Default/Sparse/Off picker fully capture what Pillar 8's stage-based cadence needs, or does the user-facing control need to expose more (or less) than what's currently drawn?; (2) is 'Sabbath/Quiet Days' the same mechanism as Pillar 8's per-stage cool-off periods, or a separate suppression layer?; (3) should this screen's copy/mode names be renamed to match Pillar 8's own vocabulary once that's locked; (6) multi-device conflicts - if these fields are ever editable from more than one signed-in device (multi-device auth isn't built yet, but is an open question elsewhere - see PRD Pillar 2 open questions), last-write-wins needs an explicit decision; (7) save failure handling - what happens if the background sync for a preference change actually fails (network drops mid-write) - silent retry, or does the user ever see an error; (8) timezone changes - Quiet Days are day-of-week based, so a user traveling across timezones could get a nudge on what they consider their quiet day; This is a cross-pillar consistency check, not yet scoped as an implementation ticket. Title: Build Prompt Architecture — Classify Today Tab Content by Online/Offline Requirement
Status: 🔄 In Progress (Mood + Life-Domain rotation built Nov 17 2026 — see note)
Notes: Raised Aug 28, 2026: Kell wants an explicit architecture classifying every Today-tab prompt/card type by whether it requires online LLM access or can run fully offline from local data. Locked classification: ONLINE-REQUIRED = contextual verse (theme-matched via Rich Context/Formation Intelligence, e.g. grief -> grief verse). OFFLINE-CAPABLE (no LLM call) = Question Bank (static rotating list, zero personalization, zero data lookup), Callback card / Continue Your Journey (pulls the user's own capture excerpt into a FIXED sentence template - personalization is which local data is selected, not any generated reasoning), On This Day (pure date-match query against local captures), Random Past Entry (pure random pick, no logic), Photo Callback (pure filter for captures with an attached photo). All four of the latter reuse the same fixed-template pattern as the callback card - none require the system to understand or reason about the content, only to select which local entry to surface. Fallback rule when offline or LLM fails: skip the contextual verse, fall back to Question Bank first (needs nothing but itself). Design pass needed: (1) formalize the fixed question-templates for On This Day / Random Past Entry / Photo Callback (currently only the main callback card's template pattern is designed); (2) write the initial Question Bank list (curated static questions, e.g. 'What's something you're carrying today that you haven't said out loud yet?'); (3) decide rotation/selection logic for Question Bank (random? day-of-week? sequential, no repeats?); (4) explicit note that upgrading any of the offline-capable types to LLM-generated (rather than templated) questions would move them into the online-required column - this is a deliberate choice, not a technical constraint. UPDATE Oct 16, 2026 session: substantial progress via docs/PILLAR_TODAY_PROMPT_TAXONOMY.md — formalized the full offline-only prompt taxonomy (Scripture, Mood, Sustain/Follow-up, Life-Domain categories locked for MVP; Rhythm/Time and Intercession moved Post-MVP except Intercession kept narrowly as the no-history fallback), a zero-LLM overlap-avoidance tagging scheme (cluster/echoes_mood/entry_id), and a 3-sub-hero-tile screen structure verified against a Figma-AI combination spec. Still open: Question Bank rotation/selection logic, and consolidating the ~13 Figma example scenarios down to the real 2-3 needed templates (Happy Path, No-History Edge Case, Error State — Error State not yet designed). UPDATE Nov 17 2026: built real rotation for 2 of the 4 MVP categories -- new TodayPromptLibraries.swift (Models/) holds the 8 locked Mood words and 5 locked Life-Domain prompts, each picked via a new shared TodayPromptRotation helper (the same day-boundary, non-repeating cache pattern DailyVerseLibrary.verseForToday() already uses, factored out so it's not reimplemented per category). TodayView's Mood and Life-Domain tiles now rotate daily instead of always showing the same hardcoded prompt; verified live on a disposable test account across two app relaunches on the same calendar day, confirming the cache holds. Still open, deliberately not touched this session: Sustain/Follow-up (needs real capture history, its own ticket-sized build), Intercession's own rotation (still a static tile -- the locked design actually wants it re-slotted as Follow-up's no-history fallback, not a 4th always-on tile, which is its own reslotting task), the cluster/echoes_mood/entry_id overlap-avoidance tagging scheme across tiles, and the Figma scenario-template consolidation + Error State design. Title: Notification Triggers Need Status-Based Checks + Sync-Based Dormancy Clock
Notes: Raised Oct 22, 2026 during P8 Notifications redesign (3-stage model: 1, 2, 3A/3B, 4A/4B). Two engineering requirements surfaced that aren't covered by any existing system design doc: (1) Stage 2/3B/4B ('journal ready' pushes) must check whether a JournalEntry record exists for the moment's ID before firing — not a timer, not an LLM call. A fallback-synthesis journal (raw transcript, per the Journal Creation fallback path) still counts as 'exists' — notification copy does not branch on synthesis success vs. fallback. (2) Stage 3A/4A/3B/4B dormancy timers must be keyed off last confirmed server sync time, not last local/offline action — paired with a hard rule that any sync event cancels a pending dormancy notification, to avoid false 'you've been quiet' pushes to users who were active offline and just hadn't synced yet. Needs to be folded into the Pillar 8 System Design FigJam board (t2FBAeGOP3PItKWzYWlHnw) and cross-referenced from T-152. Design-only decision, already locked; this ticket is the engineering follow-through, not a design task -- the stage_3b/stage_4b gap below is intentionally out of this ticket's scope until T-084 exists, so closing here rather than leaving this sitting at In Progress indefinitely. BUILT Nov 17, 2026: migration 20261117180728 adds users.last_synced_at (the dormancy clock's single source of truth -- SyncManager.touchLastSynced() stamps it after every successful sync pass, piggybacked onto the same end-of-syncPendingMoments hook T-159/T-176 already use) and notification_dormancy_log (fired-stage history, enforcing the exactly-two-cycles-lifetime rule). New SQL function due_notification_triggers() returns (user_id, trigger) pairs that are due right now -- stage_2_journal_ready (moment has a journal_entries row, regardless of synthesis vs. fallback, matching requirement 1 exactly) plus stage_3a/stage_4a dormancy (requirement 2 -- a sync resets last_synced_at to now(), which IS the 'any sync cancels a pending dormancy notification' rule, with no separate cancel bookkeeping needed). Verified live against real data (returned exactly the 11 moments-with-journal-entries rows, zero false dormancy fires for accounts active within 14 days). Caught and fixed a real security hole before considering this done: the function was initially callable via PostgREST's auto-exposed RPC by ANY signed-in or anonymous client, returning every user's data -- revoked EXECUTE from anon/authenticated/public and pinned search_path (migration 20261117181500). NOT YET DONE: stage_3b/stage_4b (the journal-nudge half of each dormancy pair) are intentionally deferred -- they depend on T-084's future scheduler recording exactly when 3A/4A were delivered, which doesn't exist yet. T-083 (APNs key, Kell generating it now) and T-084 (the actual scheduler/sender) are what turns this decision logic into a real push.

Title: Fix Groq calls silently falling back to OpenAI 100% of the time
Notes: Usage dashboard showed 100% OpenAI / 0% Groq despite T-168's locked provider decision. Root cause was a cascading model deprecation: llama3-70b-8192 (the originally wired model) had been retired by Groq; the first fix (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) ALSO 404'd ("does not exist or you do not have access to it"). Resolved by querying GET api.groq.com/openai/v1/models directly with the real GROQ_API_KEY via a temporary debug branch in the deployed function (removed after use) rather than guessing a third model name — Groq's lineup for this account has moved away from Llama chat models entirely (only prompt-guard classifiers, qwen/qwen3.8-27b, allam-2-7b, and openai/gpt-oss-* remain). Switched to openai/gpt-oss-120b (131K context, largest general-purpose option). Verify live Groq calls are landing on your next session — not yet re-confirmed after this exact fix. UPDATE Nov 11 2026: partially re-confirmed, and found a second real cause. capture_conversation calls ARE landing on Groq (confirmed via function_logs). But journal_preview_generation calls were still falling back to OpenAI on a specific, non-free-tier reason: function_logs showed 'Groq response missing choices[0].message.content' — NOT a rate-limit/quota error. gpt-oss-120b is a reasoning model that spends tokens on hidden thinking before its visible answer; at the proxy's old max_tokens:500, it sometimes burned the whole budget on reasoning and returned empty content, which the proxy correctly treated as a Groq failure. Fixed: added reasoning_effort:'low' to the Groq request (cuts how much of the budget reasoning eats) and raised DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS 500->1000. Redeployed (version 9). UPDATE Nov 11 2026 (later same day): re-verified live via public.llm_usage + function_logs. The one OpenAI fallback in the last 24h landed at 03:14:47 UTC, BEFORE the reasoning_effort/max_tokens fix deployed as llm-proxy version 9 at 03:55:53 UTC — confirmed the exact same 'Groq response missing choices[0].message.content' failure, not a new cause. Every call since the version-9 deploy (9 calls across capture_conversation, journal_synthesis, and dweller_profile_summary, spanning 04:02 UTC to 23:36 UTC) landed cleanly on Groq with zero OpenAI fallbacks. Fix confirmed working.

Title: Cap max input length per capture-conversation turn
Notes: Raised Nov 11 2026 during a design discussion on the Reflective Density Model / token-cost risk: confirmed nothing limited how much text a single capture turn sent to the LLM -- llm-proxy's DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS only caps the model's OUTPUT per call, and DAILY_CALL_LIMIT (60/day) only counts number of calls, not their size; no maxLength/character limit existed anywhere on CaptureConversationView's compose TextField. Design built first in Figma (per Kell's ask) before any code: found the file-key mixup mid-session (was referencing t5MUGEtpeFcUixobvHiYMc, an explicitly-labeled ''Existing Experience Baseline'' snapshot -- corrected to the real current file jBOzv1vO2C2DSMePqRl4c4 ''dwelly-redesign-file-important'', now documented in CLAUDE.md). Checked the file's own established error-state conventions before designing anything: E2/E3 (''Didn't catch that'') replace the compose pill's own content with a gold-bordered message -- confirmed with Kell this does NOT apply here since real typed text must stay visible/editable, not be overwritten. E6 (''Max Duration Reached'', the 10-min voice cap) uses a plain muted caption below the collapsed compose card -- confirmed this IS the right precedent to follow. Built ''E9 -- Message Too Long (Character Cap)'' via the Figma plugin API (not guessed), cloned from E6, caption swapped to ''That's a lot -- trim it down to send.'', Send button dimmed; duplicated into both P1 Capture Onboarding (node 1188:1198) and Kell's new P1b Capture Post-Onboarding page (node 1189:1216), since error/edge-case states were already established as shared across onboarding/post-onboarding (E1-E8 were never duplicated either). Implemented in CaptureConversationView.swift: maxInputLength = 2000 chars (~500 tokens at ~4 chars/token, character count used as a proxy since the real tokenizer isn't available client-side), isOverCharacterLimit computed property, Send disabled + dimmed (opacity 0.4) and sendUserTurn() guards against it defensively, caption shown below the collapsed compose card only (matches Figma; expanded/full-screen state has no room under the keyboard but Send stays disabled regardless). Title: Build DwellerProfile running summary (store + show
column9: Raised Nov 11 2026, the direct outcome of the Reflective Density Model / DwellerProfile strategy discussion: Kell weighed printing a running summary to the profile vs. also feeding it back into Dwelly's live conversation, and explicitly chose store + show only for MVP -- the feed-back option adds a small but compounding per-message cost forever, while store-and-show's cost is flat (one extra small LLM call per capture) and fully isolable, which matters because Kell plans to dogfood this extensively for a couple weeks before beta specifically to assess real cost before deciding on the feed-back question. Built: new unencrypted public.dweller_profiles table (user_id PK, running_summary text, updated_at), same direct-REST pattern as journal_entries (no new Edge Function/encryption -- it summarizes journal_entries.body, which is itself already unencrypted). DwellerProfileManager.updateRunningSummary(newEntryBody:userId:apiClient:) fires fire-and-forget from CaptureConversationView.finishAndSave() -- only on a real synthesized (approved) entry, never a pending one -- reading the current running summary (if any) + the new entry's body, asking the LLM for an updated 2-4 sentence third-person summary via the existing callLLM infra (feature: dweller_profile_summary), and upserting it. Explicitly NOT done: nothing anywhere reads this back into a capture conversation's system prompt -- CaptureConversationView is untouched beyond the one fire-and-forget call site. Built DwellerProfileView (new, minimal, linked from Settings as 'Your Profile') to show the raw summary text plus a last-updated date, with an empty state for new users -- deliberately NOT the Growth tab's future tier-gated 'Your Narrative' experience (narrativeText), which stays a separate, later, more curated thing. Verified live via a temporary debug bypass rendering both the seeded and empty states (MockAPIClient debugSeedDwellerProfile helper added, matching the existing debugSeed(moment:journalEntry:) convention), reverted cleanly (git diff confirmed clean on DwellyApp.swift before/after). Build succeeded (iPhone 17 simulator).

Title: Fix onboarding-loop bug (missing chevron) + journal synthesis length/fidelity
Notes: Raised Nov 11 2026: Kell saw the onboarding-only Continue button on what should have been an ordinary, post-onboarding capture, asking 'what are they continuing to?'. Root cause: JournalDetailView's header always rendered the back chevron regardless of onDone, even though the file's own existing comment already said the chevron should be replaced during onboarding ('there's nothing to go back TO') -- it just was never implemented. Tapping the chevron during the mandatory first capture dismisses without ever calling onDone, so completeOnboarding() never fires, and the app re-routes the NEXT capture through the onboarding first-capture flow again. Fixed: chevron is now hidden (replaced with an equal-width spacer to keep the header balanced) whenever onDone is set, forcing Continue as the only exit. Separately flagged, not yet root-caused: a direct query of public.users shows every single test account's name and onboarding_completed_at as null, suggesting the fire-and-forget background sync in ProfileManager may be silently failing more often than expected -- worth a closer look later, not blocking since local on-device state (what the app actually gates on) is independent of this. Also fixed the journal synthesis fidelity problem Kell caught comparing a real entry against what he actually said: the old prompt demanded a fixed '2-3 paragraphs' regardless of input length and explicitly said 'not a summary of a conversation' -- producing entries 2-3x longer than the real transcript, full of invented sensory/narrative detail not in the original conversation. Rewritten to require the body stay at or under the user's own actual word count (now passed in explicitly as a concrete numeric anchor, not just a vague instruction), forbid inventing details/events/imagery not actually said, and prefer reusing the user's own real phrases/excerpts over inventing new descriptive language. A short conversation should now produce a short entry; 'under 3x the input' was replaced with a hard word-count ceiling, not just softer wording. Verified the chevron fix live via a seeded debug JournalDetailView (onDone set, header correctly shows no chevron); the synthesis fidelity fix needs a real live capture + LLM call to confirm, which the session handed back to Kell to test next. Build succeeded (iPhone 17 simulator).

Title: Strip any WhisperKit bracket-tag hallucination generically (not just an enumerated list)
Notes: Raised Nov 11 2026: while verifying T-280's voice fix live, caught a real transcription artifact -- '[no audio]' landed verbatim inside a real conversation turn's text. Title: Post-onboarding conversation must not be count-capped at 3 (Done bolted onto onboarding's fixed-3 machinery wasn't enough)
Notes: Raised Nov 11 2026: Kell reviewed a real screen recording and, after extracting/reviewing it frame-by-frame, pushed back that the real issue hadn't actually been fixed -- T-282 added a Done button but never removed the thing it was supposed to replace. Verified live: post-onboarding conversation shows no counter at all, chevron+Done correct. Could not verify live that it actually continues past response 3 without stopping -- the same already-flagged compose-field automation limitation blocked sending a second message in the debug harness -- this is a logic-review-confirmed fix, not independently exercised past turn 1.

Title: Root cause: public.users had no FK to auth.users -- silently-failing captures
Notes: The real cause behind 'entries aren't populating': public.users.id never referenced auth.users.id. Every capture afterward failed its moments_user_id_fkey/journal_entries_user_id_fkey constraint silently, while the UI still showed a deceptively successful journal card. Fixed: migration adds `public.users.id REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (applied via Supabase MCP, recorded as supabase/migrations/20261116172151_cascade_delete_users_fk_and_cleanup_orphans.sql), cleaned 22 other orphaned rows; AuthManager's 3 silent print() sites routed through HTMLLogManager at ERROR level; AppView now also retries pending journal entries unconditionally on launch, not just as syncPendingMoments()'s tail call. Title: T-292's Moods fix drifted from the actual locked Figma design
Notes: T-292's own Nov 16 fix (thin-outline-always selected pills) was based on a wrong read of Kell's screenshot -- re-pulling the real Figma file (dwelly-redesign, P4 page, nodes 284:166/286:166/286:1590/280:1378) live via the Figma MCP showed selected mood chips are actually SOLID FILLED (Theme.Payment.pillBackground + textHeading text + gold checkmark), not gold-outlined; the inline Edit Entry row's selected pills were wrongly gold-outlined too (Figma: same filled style, no gold at all -- gold is reserved for the '+ Add mood' label text only, and even its dashed border is a neutral gray-blue, not gold). Also added two things Figma's design has that the code never did: the custom-mood text field now caps at 20 characters with a live 'X / 20' counter underneath (matches Mood Sheet (Typing Custom) node exactly), and existing mood pills in the inline Edit Entry row are now tappable to reopen the Mood Sheet even once at the 3-mood cap (previously the '+ Add mood' pill was the only entry point and it disappears entirely at 3/3, leaving no way back in). FOLLOW-UP (same session): Kell caught a second real gap -- the sheet's own system chrome (behind the top grabber capsule and the bottom home-indicator strip) stayed the default translucent gray material no matter what the content's background was set to, since `.background(...).ignoresSafeArea()` only paints the content layer, not the sheet's own backing layer underneath it. Fixed with `.presentationBackground(Theme.background)` (iOS 16.4+, guarded with a fallback for the 16.0 deployment target) plus `.frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)` so content fills the full sheet. Re-verified live: no gray showing anywhere in the sheet now. SECOND FOLLOW-UP (same session): Kell caught a third gap via screen recording -- toggleMood/addCustomMood mutated `selectedMoods` directly and called `persistEntry()` on every tap, so a mood change was already saved to Supabase before 'Done' was ever pressed; swiping the sheet away instead of tapping Done didn't undo anything. Added a `draftMoods` array seeded from `selectedMoods` on sheet open; toggleMood/addCustomMood now only touch the draft, and 'Done' is the one place that copies it back into `selectedMoods` (persisted afterward through the normal edit-mode Save button, same as body text). Verified live: selecting a mood then swiping the sheet away leaves the entry unchanged; selecting a mood then tapping Done adds the pill and enables Save. THIRD FOLLOW-UP (same session): Kell caught a fourth gap -- the preset grid's ForEach only ever iterated `presetMoods`, so a custom word typed into 'Add your own word' got added to draftMoods and counted toward the 3/3 cap, but never rendered as a chip anywhere in the sheet -- no way to see it was selected or tap it back off. Grid now iterates `presetMoods + draftMoods.filter { !presetMoods.contains($0) }`, so a selected custom word shows up after the presets with the same filled/checkmark styling and is tappable to remove. Verified live: typing 'Curious' and tapping Add shows it as a filled, checkmarked chip in the grid; Done carries it through to the inline Edit Entry row and Save persists it. FOURTH FOLLOW-UP (same session): Kell asked two real product questions after the above -- how many custom moods should exist, and why didn't a custom mood made on one entry show up on another. Answer to the second: it never could -- a custom word only ever lived inside that one entry's own `moods` array, with no shared store anywhere. Built one: new `custom_moods` table (user_id, word, unique per user+word, RLS scoped to auth.uid()), new APIClient methods (fetchCustomMoods/addCustomMood/deleteCustomMood, real + Mock), and `JournalDetailView` now loads the user's full custom library every time the Mood Sheet opens and merges it into the grid alongside the 8 presets; a brand-new word is held as a pending draft and only written to the table on 'Done' (same draft discipline as moods themselves -- swiping away without Done doesn't pollute the shared vocabulary either). Capped at 10 distinct custom words per user (Kell's call), enforced in `addCustomMood()` with an inline limit message. Added a real 'Custom Moods' settings row (`AccountProfileView` -- the actual live Profile tab screen, not the older unused `SettingsView`) linking to a new `ManageCustomMoodsView` that lists and deletes a user's custom words. Caught and fixed a real bug along the way: every DELETE call in `SupabaseAPIClient` (this new one and the pre-existing `permanentlyDeleteMoment`) expected to decode `EmptyResponse` from the response body, but PostgREST's default `Prefer: return=minimal` on DELETE returns a genuine 204 with zero bytes, which `JSONDecoder` cannot decode into anything -- so every DELETE was silently throwing and reporting a false 'couldn't delete' even on calls that fully succeeded server-side (confirmed via direct SQL: the row was gone either way). Fixed by short-circuiting to `EmptyResponse()` when the body is empty, in the shared `makeRequest`. Verified live end-to-end: added 'Hopeful2' on one entry, confirmed it appeared (unselected, available) on an entirely different entry's Mood Sheet; deleted it from the new Settings screen with no false error and immediate list update; added 'Grounded' fresh and confirmed the same real delete success. FIFTH FOLLOW-UP (same session): Kell didn't want a settings list row with a trash icon -- wanted this screen to read as a bigger version of the Mood Sheet's own pill chips. Redesigned `ManageCustomMoodsView` as a `LazyVGrid` of the same `Theme.Payment.pillBackground` capsule chips (17pt text, larger padding than the Mood Sheet's), with an 'x' glyph in place of the Mood Sheet's checkmark -- the action here is remove, not select. Tapping anywhere on a chip deletes it. Verified live with 3 seeded custom moods: chips render as a wrapping grid matching the Mood Sheet's visual language, tapping one removes it and the grid reflows. SIXTH FOLLOW-UP (same session): Kell reconsidered the whole separate-screen approach -- dropped the cap from 10 to 4, removed the standalone Settings screen/row entirely (deleted `ManageCustomMoodsView.swift` and its project + Settings references), and moved deletion into the Mood Sheet itself: every custom (non-preset) chip there now always shows a small 'x' next to its label, a second, independent tap target from the toggle so it still works even when the chip is capped-out/disabled (deleting one is exactly how you free a slot). Tapping it shows a confirm alert ('Delete \Grounded\"? It stays on any entry that already used it
column9: but won't be offered again.') before calling `apiClient.deleteCustomMood`. The 4-cap's limit message now points at this: 'Tap the ✕ on one below to delete it and add another.' Verified live: the x only appears on custom chips (never presets)

Title: First save right after a cold app launch can silently fail (401 before JWT refresh completes)
Notes: Found live while verifying T-294 (Nov 16 2026): the very first write call (persistEntry save, or any other authenticated POST/PATCH) made right after a fresh app launch can hit a 401 -- confirmed via simulator logs showing a 401 response on launch, before AuthManager's JWT auto-refresh has completed. persistEntry()'s `loadedEntry = try? await apiClient.saveJournalEntry(entry)` swallows the failure silently (by design, for the common case), so the UI shows the change as saved (optimistic local state) while the server never received it -- confirmed by direct SQL query showing moods=[] immediately after a save that the UI displayed as successful. The identical save, done again later in the same session (token already refreshed), persists correctly. Needs investigation into AuthManager's token-refresh timing at launch -- likely a race between the first authenticated request firing and a silent/background refresh call, rather than a hard-expired token. Next session should reproduce with simulator log capture (`log show --predicate 'process == \Dwelly\"'` ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED Nov 17 2026: refreshJWTToken() had no single-flight guard. MainTabView mounts all 4 tabs at once (opacity-toggled, not conditional), so EntriesView.onAppear, TodayView's own .task (T-188's new Journal Ready fetch included), AppView's onboarding gate, and SyncManager's connectivity monitor can all fire authenticated requests within the same instant at cold launch -- if the restored JWT is already expired, each one independently hit the 401 branch and called refreshJWTToken() separately. Supabase rotates refresh tokens on every use, so only the FIRST of those concurrent refresh calls succeeded; every other one sent an already-consumed refresh token and got rejected, surfacing as exactly this silent intermittent 401. Fixed with a shared `inFlightRefresh` task in SupabaseAPIClient -- every concurrent 401 now awaits the SAME refresh call instead of each starting its own. NOT independently reproduced live this session (needs a genuinely expired JWT at launch, which the current simulator session's fresh token didn't provide) -- confirmed via code inspection matching the ticket's own hypothesis exactly, and smoke-tested clean on a real cold launch with no regressions.
column10: then either delay first writes until a known-valid token exists
column11: or make persistEntry's failure surface instead of silently discarding the change."

Title: Smooth the keyboard->voice-recording transition in the compose surface
Notes: Raised Nov 17 2026: Kell reported tapping mic while typing produced an almost-entirely-black screen with only the 0:00 timer floating mid-screen -- read as a full screen change, not a continuous transition. Root-caused three separate gaps rather than patching with a fade/delay: (1) AudioRecordingManager flips its own `isRecording` on its own internal DispatchQueue.main.async hops, detached from any withAnimation transaction this screen's button actions set up, so unifiedComposeSurface's card snapped to its new size/position with zero animation; (2) nothing explicitly dismissed the keyboard at mic-tap time, so the capsule's Y-position (which reads live keyboardHeight) computed against the still-full keyboard height for a beat, landing it mid-screen; (3) stopping had a second gap -- isRecording goes false near-instantly but isTranscribingVoice only flips true once AVAudioRecorder's delegate confirms the file finished writing, a separate later async hop, so the capsule would briefly collapse back toward the editor and immediately re-expand -- a flicker. Fixed: handleRecordTap's start branch now sets inputFocused=false synchronously at tap time so keyboard dismissal begins immediately; added @State isRecordingAnimated mirroring audioManager.isRecording via .onChange + withAnimation (the manager's own detached mutation can't be animated at the call site, so this re-wraps the observed change in our own transaction); added @State isStoppingToTranscribe to bridge the stop-to-transcribe gap, cleared the moment transcription actually starts (with a 3s fallback timer in case the recorder's delegate never fires at all -- a pre-existing unhandled failure mode, not newly introduced); isTranscribingVoice's own two mutation sites (owned directly by this view, not by the manager) wrapped directly in withAnimation. isVoiceCapturing's geometry-driving condition now reads these animated mirrors instead of the raw manager properties; the recording-vs-transcribing content switch inside the capsule still reads the live manager value directly since that's a same-size content crossfade with no frame jump to coordinate. Verified live via a debug harness (real taps still don't land on this screen's buttons in the simulator) driving real typing, real mic start/collapse, real Stop into real on-device transcription (ambient simulator mic audio, not deliberately spoken -- one take transcribed actual ambient sound, another correctly hit the empty-transcript error path with the draft preserved), repeat-recording, and Cancel with the draft intact -- screen-recorded end to end. Could not visually confirm the capsule tracking a LIVE keyboard-dismiss animation specifically: the simulator's on-screen keyboard never appeared for this screen's programmatic `.focused()` toggle during automated testing (kb stayed 0 throughout), so that one sub-case is verified by code inspection (the existing keyboardWillHide handler's real notification-driven animation, unchanged) rather than by video. Debug hooks removed, clean build reinstalled.

Title: Today-tab prompt tiles open Capture idle instead of pre-seeded with the prompt question

The plain "+" capture path (no prompt) never surfaced this since nil was already the correct value there either way. FIXED: replaced both with one Identifiable `CaptureRequest { id, prompt }` @State, presented via .fullScreenCover(item: $captureRequest) -- same pattern `paywallContext` already used correctly elsewhere in this exact file for the identical class of problem (trigger and payload collapsed into one atomic value, nothing left to race). NOT fixed, deliberately out of scope: a successful purchase after the second-capture paywall gate still opens plain capture with no prompt restored (same pre-existing gap as before this fix, just no longer masked by the showCapture race specifically) -- would need PaywallContext or a separate pending-prompt var to carry the original prompt across that round-trip; raise separately if wanted.
